tilts.set: SET on 2026-11-13 by the Portfolio Fitness for Fighting judg

industry.why: Double Underweight, carried, with the first European consumer readings in six weeks on its side and the tape's disagreement narrower. German consumer confidence (GfK) reads -30.8 for November from -30.6 and the euro area's flash reads -17.9 for October from -16.5 (Newsquawk, undated): low and edging lower, so the condition 'to D on a European consumer reading that is not falling' is tested and not met. The United States reading is disputed (University of Michigan 51.0, a three-month high, 6 November, against outlets describing it as falling). Relative strength, 2026-11-13 against 2026-09-11, not week on week: D now, D prior at the industry (C at last week's reading), with Online retail A, Hotels B (A last week), Apparel B and Physical retail B, so the second condition (the industry at C or better with Hotels and Online retail holding A) is not met either. Component 1 regime, 13-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its 52-week high, still present on Richard's European test and weakening at the margin for the first time: breadth up a third week to 66%, 60%, 62% and 63% of stocks above the 50, 100, 150 and 200-day averages, the three longer ones still below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, cyclicals ahead of defensives over one week and twelve months while defensives lead at four weeks, three months and six months; the causes unread by any reasoned source for a second week, web headlines only, and the headlines lean against the rates squeeze of the 30-Oct-26 read: the Federal Reserve easing, oil below $100). Counter-case: the survey readings are undated headlines, four sectors still read A or B, 20 Pool stocks sit under this letter, and cyclicals led over the last week. To D on a European consumer reading that is not falling, or the industry back at C with Online retail holding A.

sector.key: H.6. Gambling - operators and B2B suppliers
sector.why: Underweight, carried with a sharper reason, on the special topic 'The UK Budget of 28-Oct-26': Machine Games Duty rises from 20% to 25% from April 2027, the third UK gambling duty rise in twelve months, justified by the Treasury on harm grounds, which makes further rises easier to repeat; April 2027 brings two steps at once (machines and 25% remote betting duty), and relief rallies have not held (Entain 772p after November 2025's relief, about 470p now). Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): discretionary spend and complex regulatory cases in a regime that sells complexity. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: F now, F prior, agrees. One live holding, Bally's Intralot (2.00%): the Evoke purchase was struck at 20% and will not be repriced, so the Budget removed a tail risk for it; whether its case is judged against this row's logic is Richard's open question, not this call's. Counter-case: gambling spend has been resilient in downturns and the market priced relief twice. To C if the April 2027 steps pass with no further rise announced and relative strength leaves F.

geography.why: Neutral, carried; the Bank of England's decision of 5-Nov-26 is still unread and the headlines disagree on it (on hold according to MarketScreener, cutting in 2026 according to the Irish Examiner, both undated); a weaker November consumer confidence headline (Trading Economics, undated) was not confirmed as a print for the window. Component 1 regime, 13-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its 52-week high, still present on Richard's European test and weakening at the margin for the first time: breadth up a third week to 66%, 60%, 62% and 63% of stocks above the 50, 100, 150 and 200-day averages, the three longer ones still below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, cyclicals ahead of defensives over one week and twelve months while defensives lead at four weeks, three months and six months; the causes unread by any reasoned source for a second week, web headlines only, and the headlines lean against the rates squeeze of the 30-Oct-26 read: the Federal Reserve easing, oil below $100). 28 Pool stocks are UK-listed and a Neutral country carries no weight in Thematic Fit/Momentum; the book is 39% UK-listed by invested weight (component 5). Balanced on unread evidence, so Neutral is an absence here, not a judgement. To D on hawkish guidance when the decision is read; to B if a second source makes the UK case with the rate path read.
